name: Workmates Core2Cloud Solution Ltd
title: Workmates Core2Cloud Solution Ltd - 544610 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Cloud/AI services firm guides FY27 revenue to INR 210 cr (+45%) with INR 190 cr visibility, but FY26 margins fell (EBITDA 16.2% vs 17.7%) and no supply-side capacity data is given.

summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 34% to INR 143 crore with 82.5% recurring; FY27 target INR 210 crore, with INR 190 crore visibility cited.
summary.overview: Workmates reported FY26 revenue of INR 143 crore (up 34%) and PAT of INR 15.92 crore (up 16%, margin 11.1% vs 13%). Margins compressed: gross margin 32.8% vs 33.9% and EBITDA margin 16.2% vs 17.7%, which management attributes to a Dubai contract exit (about INR 4 crore), a gaming client exit (INR 3.5 crore) and about INR 6 crore of added headcount cost. Management set an FY27 revenue target of INR 210 crore (45%+ growth) and entered FY27 with MRR of INR 13.5 crore per month. This was the company's first earnings call since its BSE SME listing.

financial_highlights.value: INR 218 crore as stated on call (inconsistent with 82.5% recurring share of INR 143 crore revenue)

financial_highlights.change: +16% YoY; vs INR 13.9 crore (13%) in FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR 7.58 crore at FY26 entry; INR 10 crore at FY26 exit; INR 13.5 crore at FY27 opening
financial_highlights.change: FY27 opening is 35% above FY26 exit

segments.name: Recurring / annuity services
segments.commentary: Management said 82.5% of FY26 revenue was recurring; contracted recurring base of about INR 40 crore per quarter (about INR 160 crore annualised) for FY27.

segments.name: Project implementation (transformation)
segments.commentary: Project implementation billing grew 56.3% to INR 25 crore in FY26, described as the feeder for future managed services. H1 FY27 project billing visibility is about INR 5.82 crore.

segments.name: AI services
segments.commentary: AI services revenue was about INR 2 crore of the INR 143 crore in FY26; AI plus cybersecurity targeted at about 5% of FY27 revenue. Management says AI influences much larger cloud and managed services revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target INR 210 crore (45%+ growth); contracted/visible base INR 190.56 crore, leaving about INR 19-20 crore of new business to win over ~10 months.
H1 FY27 outlook about INR 91.56 crore (about INR 79-80 crore contracted, INR 6.15 crore recurring new, INR 5.82 crore project implementation); H2 estimate about INR 99 crore.
FY27 PAT guided at about INR 24-25 crore on INR 210 crore revenue; management said PAT margin would be similar to or higher than FY26 margin.
Margin recovery levers: higher AI and security mix, billable utilisation from 84% toward 88%, and operating leverage as new hires reach full productivity.
FY27 target excludes any US or UK turnover. AI expected to be a meaningful contributor in FY27 and the primary growth engine from FY28.
capex_capacity: Manpower cost about INR 16.9-17 crore on about 170 employees (about INR 9-10 lakh per head); FY27 existing-staff cost expected to rise to INR 18.5-19 crore with appraisals plus about INR 1.5 crore of new hires.
Three delivery centres (Kolkata, Bhubaneswar, Hyderabad); nine locations in total. 120+ AWS-certified professionals out of 170+ staff.

US billing entity setup initiated; full US office and Singapore expansion contingent on geopolitical situation. Management said a light, fractional-consultant model will be used for global acquisition.
IntelliOps AI operations platform onboarded for more than 60% (later stated 65-70%) of customers; management intends to list it on the AWS marketplace.
demand_pricing: Management described competition as spanning TCS, Infosys and Accenture, Big Four firms, and mid-size cloud peers such as Minfy and Rapyder. Differentiators cited: AWS premier-tier partner status (less than 1% of AWS partners globally), Gen-AI competency, and the highest count of AWS competencies in India.

Pipeline includes Agentic AI platform migration, Gen-AI and data analytics in manufacturing, AI-led transformation for a large insurer, fintech cloud migrations and an NBFC cloud implementation. Management said 7-8 enterprise deals were targeted for closure in Q2.
Enterprise client count rose from 34 to 38; 28 net new clients added; top 20 accounts contributed 73% of revenue; client retention 95%. Management said top-5 concentration has declined.

Management said customers negotiate hard on managed-services and implementation pricing in India, while accepting AWS consumption costs. Hardware prices reportedly doubled or tripled, which management views as a tailwind for cloud migration.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of the INR 210 crore FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Anirban Dasgupta said about INR 160 crore is contracted (INR 40 crore per quarter), plus INR 30 crore visibility, giving INR 190.56 crore; the remaining about INR 19 crore must be won over 10 months.

qa_highlights.question: What PAT margin is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Debasish Sarkar said PAT margin would be around the same or higher, equating to about INR 24-25 crore PAT on INR 210 crore revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will manpower cost rise as revenue scales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bulk of practice investments are done; existing staff cost goes to about INR 18.5-19 crore with appraisals plus about INR 1.5 crore of new hires. AI tools are expected to let the same headcount deliver more projects.

qa_highlights.question: Is there hardware or GPU cost pass-through risk on annuity contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Anirban Dasgupta said AWS prices have stayed flat or fallen, the platform provides GPU and LLM infrastructure via Bedrock, and there is no cost surprise in existing revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI revenue share and is it linked to cloud?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 pure AI services revenue was about INR 2 crore; AI plus cybersecurity targeted at about 5% of FY27 revenue; AI typically pulls through cloud and managed services.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Dubai contract declined?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamal Nath said credit-insurance checks failed for the customer and the replacement entity; the INR 1 crore per month order (about INR 12 crore) was declined on bad-debt risk.

risks_watch: Revenue visibility gap: about INR 19-20 crore of new book-and-bill must be won within about 10 months to reach INR 210 crore.
Margin compression in FY26 (gross margin down 110 bps, EBITDA down 150 bps); FY27 recovery depends on utilisation rising from 84% to 88% and new hires reaching productivity.
Inconsistent recurring revenue figure: management cited INR 218 crore recurring revenue alongside INR 143 crore total revenue and an 82.5% recurring share. Needs clarification.
Global expansion (US entity, Singapore scale-up) is contingent on geopolitical conditions and would add cost before revenue; management said it is excluded from FY27 target.
Concentration of 73% revenue in top 20 accounts; Dubai and gaming exits show credit and client-quality risk.
Q2 FY27 enterprise deal closures (7-8 deals targeted) are a key checkpoint.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the FY27 target and AI positioning, with specific visibility figures, but cautious on international expansion, which management tied to geopolitical conditions. Some answers were loose on numbers (recurring revenue and H1 figures were inconsistent), so the call should be read with that in mind.
key_quotes: Our FY27 revenue target is INR 210 crores, a 45% plus growth on FY26.
We are a premier-tier partner, which is the highest level of partnership.
AI will be a meaningful contributor in FY27, and our primary growth engine from FY28 onwards.

growth.why: FY27 revenue target of INR 210 crore (+45%) is backed by INR 190.56 crore contracted/visible base (about 90% of target), with about INR 19-20 crore left to win; no new capacity additions were quantified, and utilisation is 84% moving toward 88%.
